brihadaranyaka-1-1-1.translation: The dawn is the head of the sacrificial horse, the sun its eye, the wind its breath, the universal fire its open mouth, the year its body. Heaven is its back, the mid-air its belly, the earth its hoof-rest, the directions its sides, the in-between directions its ribs, the seasons its limbs, the months and half-months its joints, days and nights its feet, the stars its bones, the clouds its flesh. Sand is the food in its stomach, rivers its intestines, mountains its liver and lungs, plants and trees its hair. The rising sun is its front half, the setting sun its back half. When it yawns, lightning flashes; when it shakes, it thunders; when it urinates, it rains. Speech is its neigh.
brihadaranyaka-1-1-1.meaning: The whole universe is pictured as the body of the sacred horse.
brihadaranyaka-1-1-1.explanation: The Brihadaranyaka, the 'Great Forest Upanishad', opens by turning the horse sacrifice into a meditation on the cosmos.

brihadaranyaka-1-1-2.translation: The day was born as the glory in front of the horse; its source is the eastern sea. The night was born as the glory behind it; its source is the western sea. These two glories came to be on either side of the horse. As 'haya' it carried the gods, as 'vajin' the gandharvas, as 'arvan' the demons, as 'ashva' humans. The sea is its kin, the sea its source.
brihadaranyaka-1-1-2.meaning: Day and night are the two glories of the cosmic horse, born from the eastern and western seas.
brihadaranyaka-1-1-2.explanation: Different names for the horse match the beings it carries.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-1.translation: In the beginning there was nothing here at all. This was covered by death, by hunger, for hunger is death. Death thought, 'Let me have a self.' It moved about worshipping. From its worship water was born. 'While I worshipped, water (ka) came to me,' it thought. That is why fire is called arka. Water comes to one who knows this.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-1.meaning: In the beginning there was only death, which is hunger; from its wish for a self, water was born.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-1.explanation: A creation story where death and hunger come first. Arka (fire, praise) is linked to arcat (worshipping) and ka (water, joy).

brihadaranyaka-1-2-2.translation: Water is arka. The froth on the water hardened and became the earth. Death toiled on it, and from its toil and heat its essence of light came out as fire.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-2.meaning: The froth of the waters became earth, and from death's effort came fire.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-2.explanation: Creation continues: earth from water, fire from effort.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-3.translation: It divided itself three ways: fire as a third, the sun as a third, wind as a third. This is breath, divided three ways. The east is its head; the north-east and south-east its arms; the west its tail; the north-west and south-west its thighs; south and north its sides; heaven its back; the mid-air its belly; this earth its chest. It rests on water. One who knows this has firm footing wherever he goes.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-3.meaning: Life divided itself into fire, sun and wind, and the world is its body.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-3.explanation: The cosmos as a living creature again.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-4.translation: It wished, 'Let a second self be born to me.' Death, hunger, united speech with mind. The seed became the year; before that there was no year. It carried him for as long as a year, then gave birth. When he was born, death opened its mouth to eat him. He cried 'bhan!' That became speech.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-4.meaning: Death longed for a second self and gave birth to the year; the newborn's cry became speech.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-4.explanation: Time itself is born from death, and speech from the first cry.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-5.translation: He thought, 'If I kill him, I will have less food.' With that speech and that self he created everything here: Rik verses, Yajus formulas, Saman chants, metres, sacrifices, people and animals. Whatever he created he began to eat. Because he eats (atti) everything, Aditi is called Aditi. One who knows this becomes the eater of everything, and everything becomes his food.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-5.meaning: Instead of eating the newborn, death created all things and began to eat them all.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-5.explanation: Death is the eater of all; word-play on Aditi and atti, 'eats'.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-6.translation: He wished, 'Let me sacrifice again with a greater sacrifice.' He toiled and practised austerity. From him, toiling and heated, glory and vigour went out. Glory and vigour are the life-breaths. When the breaths had left, his body began to swell. But his mind was still in his body.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-6.meaning: Through effort his life-breaths left him and his body swelled, though his mind remained.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-6.explanation: This prepares the explanation of the horse sacrifice's name.

brihadaranyaka-1-2-7.translation: He wished, 'Let this body be fit for sacrifice; let me have a self through it.' So it became a horse (ashva). Because it swelled (ashvat), it became fit for sacrifice (medhya); that is why the horse sacrifice is called ashvamedha. One who knows it so truly knows the horse sacrifice. He let it roam free and after a year sacrificed it to himself, giving the other animals to the gods. That one who shines is the horse sacrifice; the year is its body. This fire is arka; these worlds are its body. Fire and horse sacrifice are one deity, death. One who knows this conquers repeated death; death does not reach him, death becomes his self, he lives a full life and becomes one with these deities.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-7.meaning: The swelling body became the horse; knowing this conquers death.
brihadaranyaka-1-2-7.explanation: Word-play on ashva (horse) and ashvat (swelled). The sun is the true horse sacrifice.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-1.translation: There were two kinds of Prajapati's children, gods and demons. The gods were the younger, the demons the elder. They competed for these worlds. The gods said, 'Let us overcome the demons through the udgitha chant at the sacrifice.'
brihadaranyaka-1-3-1.meaning: Gods and demons, both children of the creator, fought for the worlds; the gods chose the sacred chant as their weapon.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-1.explanation: A story about breath, also told in Chandogya 1.2.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-2.translation: Then they said to speech, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and speech sang for them. The enjoyment in speech it sang for the gods; the good says it kept for itself. The demons knew, 'Through this singer they will overcome us.' They rushed at it and pierced it with evil. That evil is the wrong things one says.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-2.meaning: Speech sang for the gods, but the demons spoiled it with evil; that is why we sometimes says wrongly.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-2.explanation: The gods try each power to sing the sacred chant against the demons. Each one is spoiled because it keeps something for itself.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-3.translation: Then they said to the breath of smell, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and the breath of smell sang for them. The enjoyment in the breath of smell it sang for the gods; the good smells it kept for itself. The demons knew, 'Through this singer they will overcome us.' They rushed at it and pierced it with evil. That evil is the wrong things one smells.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-3.meaning: The breath of smell sang for the gods, but the demons spoiled it with evil; that is why we sometimes smells wrongly.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-3.explanation: The gods try each power to sing the sacred chant against the demons. Each one is spoiled because it keeps something for itself.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-4.translation: Then they said to the eye, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and the eye sang for them. The enjoyment in the eye it sang for the gods; the good sees it kept for itself. The demons knew, 'Through this singer they will overcome us.' They rushed at it and pierced it with evil. That evil is the wrong things one sees.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-4.meaning: The eye sang for the gods, but the demons spoiled it with evil; that is why we sometimes sees wrongly.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-4.explanation: The gods try each power to sing the sacred chant against the demons. Each one is spoiled because it keeps something for itself.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-5.translation: Then they said to the ear, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and the ear sang for them. The enjoyment in the ear it sang for the gods; the good hears it kept for itself. The demons knew, 'Through this singer they will overcome us.' They rushed at it and pierced it with evil. That evil is the wrong things one hears.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-5.meaning: The ear sang for the gods, but the demons spoiled it with evil; that is why we sometimes hears wrongly.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-5.explanation: The gods try each power to sing the sacred chant against the demons. Each one is spoiled because it keeps something for itself.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-6.translation: Then they said to the mind, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and the mind sang for them. The enjoyment in the mind it sang for the gods; the good it imagines it kept for itself. The demons pierced it with evil; that evil is the wrong things one imagines. So they struck these deities with evils and pierced them with evil.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-6.meaning: The mind too was spoiled by evil; that is why we imagine wrong things.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-6.explanation: All five powers fail because they keep part of the reward for themselves.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-7.translation: Then they said to the breath in the mouth, 'Sing the chant for us.' 'Very well,' and this breath sang for them. The demons knew, 'Through this singer they will overcome us.' They rushed at it, wanting to pierce it with evil. But as a clod of earth striking a rock is shattered, so they were shattered and scattered in all directions and perished. So the gods prospered and the demons were defeated. One who knows this prospers, and his hateful rival is defeated.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-7.meaning: The breath of life could not be spoiled; the demons broke against it like clods against a rock.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-7.explanation: The central breath (prana) keeps nothing for itself, so evil cannot touch it.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-8.translation: They said, 'Where was the one who stood by us like this?' 'He is here within the mouth (ayam asye).' He is Ayasya Angirasa, for he is the essence (rasa) of the limbs (anga).
brihadaranyaka-1-3-8.meaning: The breath that saved them lives in the mouth and is the essence of the body.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-8.explanation: Word-play: Ayasya (in the mouth) and Angirasa (essence of the limbs).

brihadaranyaka-1-3-9.translation: This deity is called Dur, for death is far (dura) from it. Death is far from one who knows this.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-9.meaning: This breath is far from death, and so is the one who knows it.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-9.explanation: Another name for breath, linked to 'far'.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-10.translation: This deity took away the evil, the death, of these deities and sent it to where the directions end, and left their evils there. So one should not go to people there or to that end, lest one meet evil, death.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-10.meaning: Breath carried away evil and death to the edge of the world.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-10.explanation: An old belief that the far edges of the world are places of ill fortune.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-11.translation: Having taken away the evil, the death, of these deities, this deity carried them beyond death.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-11.meaning: Breath then carried all the senses beyond death.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-11.explanation: Each sense is now freed in turn.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-12.translation: Then it carried speech first. When speech across. When speech first. When speech was freed from death, it became fire. That fire, having passed beyond death, shines.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-12.meaning: Freed from death, speech first. When speech became fire.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-12.explanation: Breath carries each power beyond death, where it becomes its cosmic form.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-13.translation: Then it carried breath (smell) across. When breath (smell) was freed from death, it became wind. That wind, having passed beyond death, blows.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-13.meaning: Freed from death, breath (smell) became wind.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-13.explanation: Breath carries each power beyond death, where it becomes its cosmic form.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-14.translation: Then it carried the eye across. When the eye was freed from death, it became the sun. That the sun, having passed beyond death, burns.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-14.meaning: Freed from death, the eye became the sun.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-14.explanation: Breath carries each power beyond death, where it becomes its cosmic form.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-15.translation: Then it carried the ear across. When the ear was freed from death, it became the directions. That the directions, having passed beyond death, stretch out.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-15.meaning: Freed from death, the ear became the directions.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-15.explanation: Breath carries each power beyond death, where it becomes its cosmic form.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-16.translation: Then it carried the mind across. When the mind was freed from death, it became the moon. That moon, having passed beyond death, shines. So this deity carries beyond death one who knows this.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-16.meaning: Freed from death, the mind became the moon; the knower too is carried beyond death.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-16.explanation: Each human power, freed, becomes a light of nature.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-17.translation: Then it sang food for itself, for whatever food is eaten is eaten by breath alone, and it rests here.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-17.meaning: Breath sang to win food, since all food is eaten by breath.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-17.explanation: Breath keeps the body alive through food.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-18.translation: The gods said, 'All this is food, and you have sung it for yourself. Give us a share in this food.' 'Then enter into me.' 'Very well,' and they settled all around it. So whatever food one eats with breath satisfies them. One who knows this becomes the support of his people, their best and their leader, an eater of food and a ruler. Whoever tries to rival such a knower among his own people is not able to support his dependants; but whoever follows him is able to support them.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-18.meaning: The senses asked for a share of food and entered breath; so eating feeds them all.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-18.explanation: Breath feeds every sense; the knower likewise becomes the support of his family.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-19.translation: He is Ayasya Angirasa, for he is the essence of the limbs. Breath is the essence of the limbs. Yes, breath is the essence of the limbs. That is why whatever limb breath leaves dries up, for it is the essence of the limbs.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-19.meaning: Breath is the life of every limb; where it leaves, the limb withers.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-19.explanation: A simple proof of breath's importance.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-20.translation: He is also Brihaspati. Speech is brihati, and he is its lord (pati); so he is Brihaspati.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-20.meaning: Breath is the lord of speech, called Brihaspati.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-21.translation: He is also Brahmanaspati. Speech is brahman, and he is its lord; so he is Brahmanaspati.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-21.meaning: Breath is also the lord of sacred speech.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-21.explanation: Brahman here means the sacred word.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-22.translation: He is also the Saman. Speech is 'sa' and he is 'ama'; that is why the Saman is called Saman. Or because he is equal (sama) to a gnat, equal to a mosquito, equal to an elephant, equal to these three worlds, equal to all this, he is the Saman. One who knows this Saman gains union with it and lives in its world.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-22.meaning: Breath is the Saman chant, equal in every creature, small or great.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-22.explanation: Breath is the same in a gnat and an elephant.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-23.translation: He is also the udgitha. Breath is 'ut', for by breath all this is held up (uttabdha); speech is 'githa', song. 'Ut' and 'githa' together make udgitha.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-23.meaning: The chant is breath holding up the song of speech.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-23.explanation: Breath and speech together make the sacred chant.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-24.translation: So Brahmadatta Chaikitaneya, while drinking Soma, said, 'May this Soma make my head fall off if Ayasya Angirasa sang the chant with anything other than this; for he sang only with speech and breath.'
brihadaranyaka-1-3-24.meaning: A priest swears that the chant is sung with nothing but speech and breath.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-25.translation: One who knows the wealth of this Saman gains wealth. Its wealth is tone. So one who is about to perform priestly duties should wish for a good tone in his voice, and perform them with a voice rich in tone. That is why people want to see a priest with a good voice at a sacrifice, like one who has wealth. One who knows this wealth of the Saman gains wealth.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-25.meaning: The wealth of the chant is its tone; a good voice is a priest's treasure.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-26.translation: One who knows the gold of this Saman gains gold. Its gold is tone. One who knows this gold of the Saman gains gold.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-26.meaning: The chant's gold is also its tone.

brihadaranyaka-1-3-27.translation: One who knows the foundation of this Saman stands firm. Its foundation is speech, for it is in speech that this breath is sung, firmly established. Some say it is food.
brihadaranyaka-1-3-27.explanation: The section ends with a small note of disagreement.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-1.translation: In the beginning this was the Self alone, in the shape of a person. Looking around, he saw nothing but himself. He first said, 'I am.' So the word 'I' came about. That is why even now, when someone is called, he first says 'It is I,' and then gives whatever other name he has. Because before all this he burned up (aushat) all evils, he is called purusha. One who knows this burns up whoever wants to come before him.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-1.meaning: In the beginning was only the Self, who first said 'I am.'
brihadaranyaka-1-4-1.explanation: A famous creation story: the first word was 'I'.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-2.translation: He was afraid; so a person alone is afraid. Then he thought, 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' Then his fear went away. What was there to fear? Fear comes only from a second.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-2.meaning: Alone, he felt fear, but realised there was nothing else to fear; fear only comes from another.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-2.explanation: A deep insight: when one sees there is no 'other', fear disappears.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-3.translation: He had no joy; so a person alone has no joy. He wished for a second. He became as large as a man and woman in close embrace. He split himself in two; from that came husband and wife. So, as Yajnavalkya said, each of us is like half of a split pea. So this space is filled by a wife. He united with her, and from that humans were born.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-3.meaning: Lonely, he split into man and woman, and from them humans were born.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-3.explanation: A creation story of love and union. Each partner is half of a whole.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-4.translation: She thought, 'How can he unite with me after producing me from himself? Let me hide.' She became a cow, he a bull; they united and cattle were born. She became a mare, he a stallion; she a female donkey, he a male donkey; they united and one-hoofed animals were born. She became a she-goat, he a he-goat; she a ewe, he a ram; they united and goats and sheep were born. So he created every pair there is, down to the ants.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-4.meaning: She hid in many forms, and he followed in matching forms, creating all the animals.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-4.explanation: A playful myth explaining the variety of creatures.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-5.translation: He knew, 'I am creation, for I created all this.' So he became creation. One who knows this lives in his creation.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-5.meaning: He realised that he himself was all of creation.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-5.explanation: The creator and the creation are one.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-6.translation: Then he churned like this, and from his mouth, as from a womb, and with his hands, he created fire. So both of these are hairless on the inside. When people say 'Worship this god, worship that god', each god is his creation, for he is all the gods. Whatever is moist he created from semen; that is Soma. All this is just food and eater: Soma is food, fire is eater. This is Brahman's higher creation, for he created gods better than himself, and though mortal he created immortals.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-6.meaning: He created fire and Soma; all gods are really his creation.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-6.explanation: All the many gods are forms of the one Self.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-7.translation: At that time all this was undifferentiated. It became differentiated by name and form: 'He has this name and this form.' Even now it is differentiated by name and form. He entered into it up to the tips of the nails, like a razor in its case or fire in firewood. People do not see him, for he is incomplete as seen in parts. Breathing, he is called breath; speaking, speech; seeing, eye; hearing, ear; thinking, mind. These are only names for his actions. Whoever worships one of these does not know, for he is incomplete in each. One should worship him as the Self, for in it all these become one. The Self is the trace of all this, for by it one knows all this, as one finds an animal by its footprints. One who knows this finds fame and praise.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-7.meaning: The Self entered everything; each sense shows only part of it, so worship the whole Self.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-7.explanation: A key teaching: the Self is hidden in all things, and we see only its parts through our senses.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-8.translation: This Self is dearer than a son, dearer than wealth, dearer than anything else, for it is innermost. If someone says something else is dearer than the Self, one may answer, 'What you hold dear will die,' and so it will. One should worship the Self alone as dear. Whoever worships the Self alone as dear, what is dear to him does not perish.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-8.meaning: The Self is dearer than children or wealth, because it is our innermost being.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-8.explanation: Everything else we love can be lost; the Self cannot.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-9.translation: People say: 'Since people think they will become everything through knowledge of Brahman, what did Brahman know by which it became everything?'
brihadaranyaka-1-4-9.meaning: How did Brahman itself become everything?
brihadaranyaka-1-4-9.explanation: A question introduces the answer in the next verse.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-10.translation: In the beginning this was Brahman. It knew itself alone: 'I am Brahman.' So it became everything. Whoever among the gods awoke to this became it; so too among the sages and among humans. Seeing this, the sage Vamadeva declared, 'I was Manu, and the sun.' Even now, whoever knows 'I am Brahman' becomes all this. Even the gods cannot stop him, for he becomes their Self. But whoever worships another deity, thinking 'He is one and I am another', does not know. He is like a domestic animal for the gods. As many animals serve a man, so each person serves the gods. If even one animal is taken away it is unpleasant, how much more if many! So the gods do not like people to know this.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-10.meaning: Brahman knew itself as 'I am Brahman' and became everything; whoever knows this becomes everything too.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-10.explanation: 'Aham brahmasmi', 'I am Brahman', is one of the four great sayings (mahavakyas). Seeing oneself as separate from the divine keeps one small.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-11.translation: In the beginning this was Brahman, one only. Being one, it did not flourish. It created a higher form, the ruling power: those who rule among the gods, Indra, Varuna, Soma, Rudra, Parjanya, Yama, Mrityu and Ishana. So there is nothing higher than the ruling power; at the royal consecration the priest sits below the king. Yet the priestly power is the source of the ruling power. So even if a king rises to the top, in the end he relies on the priestly power as his source. Whoever harms it harms his own source and becomes worse, as one who harms someone greater.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-11.meaning: Brahman created ruling power, but priestly wisdom remains its source.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-11.explanation: The classes of society are traced to Brahman's creative unfolding. Rulers must respect wisdom.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-12.translation: Still it did not flourish. It created the common people, the gods who are named in groups: the Vasus, the Rudras, the Adityas, the All-gods and the Maruts.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-12.meaning: Next Brahman created the people, matched by groups of gods.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-12.explanation: The Vaishya class, the people, mirrored in the group gods.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-13.translation: Still it did not flourish. It created the Shudra class, Pushan. This earth is Pushan, for she nourishes everything there is.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-13.meaning: Then Brahman created the class of workers, linked to the earth that nourishes all.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-13.explanation: Pushan, 'nourisher', is the earth that feeds everyone.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-14.translation: Still it did not flourish. It created a higher form, dharma, justice. Dharma is the power over the ruling power; so there is nothing higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can prevail over a strong one, as with the help of a king. Dharma is truth. So when someone speaks the truth, people say 'He speaks dharma', and when someone speaks dharma they say 'He speaks the truth'. Both are the same.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-14.meaning: Above all power stands dharma, justice, which is the same as truth; through it the weak can stand against the strong.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-14.explanation: A key verse: law and truth are higher than any ruler.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-15.translation: So there are the priestly, ruling, common and Shudra classes. Among the gods Brahman became fire; among humans, the priest; and through the others, the others. So people seek a world among the gods through fire and among humans through the priest. But whoever leaves this world without seeing his own world, the Self, is not served by it, just as the Veda unrecited or a work undone. Even if someone who does not know this does a great holy work, it will finally run out. One should worship the Self alone as one's world. Whoever does so, his work never runs out, for from this Self he creates whatever he desires.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-15.meaning: All good works eventually run out; only the Self is an unfailing world.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-15.explanation: Ritual merit is limited; knowledge of the Self is not.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-16.translation: This Self is a world for all beings. When he offers and sacrifices, he is a world for the gods. When he recites the Veda, for the sages. When he offers to the ancestors and wishes for children, for the ancestors. When he gives shelter and food to people, for humans. When he finds grass and water for animals, for animals. When beasts and birds, down to ants, live off his house, he is a world for them. As one wishes safety for one's own world, so all beings wish safety for one who knows this. This has been known and examined.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-16.meaning: A good householder supports gods, sages, ancestors, people and animals, and all beings wish him well.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-16.explanation: This passage grounds the 'five great sacrifices' of daily life: to gods, sages, ancestors, humans and animals.

brihadaranyaka-1-4-17.translation: In the beginning this was the Self alone. He wished, 'Let me have a wife, then children; let me have wealth, then do works.' That is the extent of desire; even if one wished, one would not find more. So even now a single person wishes, 'Let me have a wife, children, wealth and works.' Until he gets each one, he feels incomplete. His completeness is this: the mind is his self, speech his wife, breath his children, the eye his human wealth, for by the eye one finds it; the ear his divine wealth, for by it one hears; the body his work, for by it one works. This is the fivefold sacrifice; fivefold is the animal, fivefold the person, fivefold all this. Whoever knows this gains all this.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-17.meaning: We long for spouse, children, wealth and work, but we already have all of them within ourselves.
brihadaranyaka-1-4-17.explanation: Completeness is found inside: mind, speech, breath, eye and ear are our family and wealth.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-1.translation: 'When the father produced the seven foods by wisdom and austerity, one was common to all, two he gave the gods, three he made for himself, one he gave to the animals. On it rests everything, what breathes and what does not. Why do they not run out, though always eaten? Whoever knows their imperishability eats food with his mouth, goes to the gods and lives on strength.' These are the verses.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-1.meaning: The creator made seven kinds of food; they never run out, and the verses ask why.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-1.explanation: A riddle about food, explained in the following verses.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-2.translation: 'One was common to all': this is the food that is eaten. Whoever worships it alone is not free from wrong, for it is mixed. 'Two he gave the gods': the offering and the oblation; so people offer to the gods. Some say they are the new and full moon rites; so one should not sacrifice only for wishes. 'One he gave to animals': that is milk, for people and animals first live on milk. So a newborn is first given ghee or the breast, and a calf is called 'not yet a grass-eater'. 'On it rests everything': all rests on milk. Some say one who offers milk for a year conquers repeated death; do not think so: one who knows this conquers it the very day he offers. 'Why do they not run out?': the person is their imperishability, for he produces food again and again by thought and work. 'He eats food with his mouth': 'pratika' means mouth. 'He goes to the gods and lives on strength' is praise.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-2.meaning: The verse is explained: food never runs out because people keep making it through thought and work.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-2.explanation: A line-by-line explanation of the riddle.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-3.translation: 'Three he made for himself': mind, speech and breath. People say, 'My mind was elsewhere, I did not see; my mind was elsewhere, I did not hear,' for one sees and hears with the mind. Desire, will, doubt, faith, lack of faith, steadiness, unsteadiness, shame, understanding and fear are all mind. So even when touched from behind one knows it by the mind. Whatever sound there is, that is speech, for it reaches an end, but it is not an end. In-breath, out-breath, diffused breath, upward breath, balancing breath: all these are breath. The Self is made of these: of speech, mind and breath.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-3.meaning: Mind, speech and breath are the three foods the creator kept for himself; we are made of them.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-3.explanation: A clear description of the mind as the seat of all feelings.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-4.translation: These three are the three worlds: speech is this world, mind is the mid-air, breath is that world (heaven).
brihadaranyaka-1-5-4.meaning: Speech, mind and breath match earth, sky and heaven.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-4.explanation: The three foods are mapped onto the cosmos.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-5.translation: These three are the three Vedas: speech is the Rig Veda, mind the Yajur Veda, breath the Sama Veda.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-5.meaning: Speech, mind and breath match the three Vedas.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-5.explanation: The same triad applied to the Vedas.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-6.translation: These three are gods, ancestors and humans: speech is the gods, mind the ancestors, breath humans.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-6.meaning: They also match gods, ancestors and people.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-7.translation: These three are father, mother and child: mind is the father, speech the mother, breath the child.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-7.meaning: Mind is father, speech mother, breath their child.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-7.explanation: A family image for our inner powers.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-8.translation: Whatever is known is a form of speech, for speech is known. Speech protects him by becoming that.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-8.meaning: What is known belongs to speech.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-8.explanation: Speech, mind and breath match the known, the knowable and the unknown.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-9.translation: Whatever is still to be known is a form of mind, for mind is still to be known. Mind protects him by becoming that.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-9.meaning: What is still to be known belongs to mind.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-9.explanation: Speech, mind and breath match the known, the knowable and the unknown.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-10.translation: Whatever is unknown is a form of breath, for breath is unknown. Breath protects him by becoming that.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-10.meaning: What is unknown belongs to breath.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-10.explanation: Speech, mind and breath match the known, the knowable and the unknown.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-11.translation: Earth is the body of speech; this fire is its form of light. As far as speech extends, so far extends the earth, so far this fire.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-11.meaning: Speech has earth as its body and fire as its light.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-11.explanation: Each inner power has a body and a light in nature.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-12.translation: Heaven is the body of the mind; that sun is its form of light. As far as the mind extends, so far heaven, so far the sun. These two united, and from them breath was born. That is Indra. He has no rival, for a rival is a second. One who knows this has no rival.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-12.meaning: Mind is heaven and sun; from mind and speech, breath was born, without rival.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-12.explanation: Breath (Indra) is the child of mind and speech.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-13.translation: Water is the body of breath; that moon is its form of light. As far as breath extends, so far water, so far the moon. All these are equal, all are endless. Whoever worships them as finite wins a finite world; whoever worships them as endless wins an endless world.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-13.meaning: Breath's body is water and its light the moon; see them as endless and you win the endless.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-13.explanation: How we see things shapes what we gain.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-14.translation: This Prajapati is the year, with sixteen parts. His nights are fifteen parts; the sixteenth is constant. By the nights he grows and wanes. On the new-moon night he enters with that sixteenth part into everything that breathes, and is born again the next morning. So on that night one should not take the life of any creature, not even a lizard, in honour of that deity.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-14.meaning: The creator, like the moon, has sixteen parts; on the new-moon night he lives in all beings, so harm none that night.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-14.explanation: A lunar teaching with an ethical rule of non-harm.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-15.translation: The Prajapati who is the year with sixteen parts is a person who knows this. His wealth is fifteen parts; his Self is the sixteenth. By wealth he grows and wanes. The Self is the hub, wealth the rim. So even if he loses everything, if he lives with his Self, people say he has only lost his rim.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-15.meaning: Wealth comes and goes like the rim of a wheel; the Self is the hub that remains.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-15.explanation: A comforting image: loss of property is not loss of self.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-16.translation: There are three worlds: the world of humans, the world of ancestors and the world of gods. The human world is won only through a son, not by any other work; the ancestors' world by works; the gods' world by knowledge. The gods' world is the best of worlds, so knowledge is praised.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-16.meaning: Children, works and knowledge win three different worlds; knowledge wins the best.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-17.translation: Now the handing over. When a man thinks he is about to die, he says to his son, 'You are Brahman; you are the sacrifice; you are the world.' The son replies, 'I am Brahman; I am the sacrifice; I am the world.' All that has been learned is one in 'Brahman'; all sacrifices are one in 'sacrifice'; all worlds are one in 'world'. 'This is all. Being all this, may he support me from this world.' So a son who has been taught is said to lead to the world, and so they teach him. When one who knows this leaves this world, he enters his son with his breaths. If he has done anything wrong, the son frees him from it all; hence the name 'son' (putra). Through his son he stands firm in this world, and the divine, immortal breaths enter him.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-17.meaning: A dying father hands his learning, duties and world to his son.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-17.explanation: A tender ritual of passing on one's life's work.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-18.translation: Divine speech from earth and fire enters him. That is divine speech, by which whatever one says comes true.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-18.meaning: The father receives divine speech, whose words always come true.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-18.explanation: After handing over, the father is filled with divine powers.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-19.translation: Divine mind from heaven and the sun enters him. That is divine mind, by which one is only joyful and never sorrows.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-19.meaning: He receives a divine mind, always joyful.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-20.translation: Divine breath from water and the moon enters him. That is divine breath, which, moving or not moving, is never troubled or harmed. One who knows this becomes the Self of all beings. As that deity is, so is he. As all beings care for that deity, so all beings care for one who knows this. Whatever sorrow these creatures have stays with them; only good goes to him. Evil never goes to the gods.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-20.meaning: He receives divine breath, becomes the Self of all, and only good reaches him.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-20.explanation: The knower becomes one with the life of all beings.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-21.translation: Now a reflection on vows. Prajapati created the functions. Once created, they competed with one another. Speech vowed, 'I will speak'; the eye, 'I will see'; the ear, 'I will hear'; and so the other functions. Death, as weariness, seized them and held them back. So speech grows weary, the eye grows weary, the ear grows weary. But death did not seize the breath in the middle. They wanted to know it: 'This is the best of us, which moving or not moving is never troubled or harmed. Let us all take its form.' So they all took its form, and are called 'breaths'. The family in which one who knows this is born is named after him. Whoever competes with one who knows this withers and dies in the end. So much about the self.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-21.meaning: The senses tire, but breath never does; so all senses became forms of breath.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-21.explanation: Like Chandogya 5.1: breath is the untiring centre of life.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-22.translation: Now about the gods. Fire vowed, 'I will burn'; the sun, 'I will give heat'; the moon, 'I will shine'; and so the other gods. As breath is among the breaths, so wind is among these gods. The other gods set, but not the wind. The wind is the deity that never sets.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-22.meaning: Among the gods of nature, wind never sets, just as breath never tires.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-22.explanation: Wind is the outer counterpart of breath.

brihadaranyaka-1-5-23.translation: There is this verse: 'From where the sun rises and where it sets.' It rises from breath and sets in breath. 'The gods made it their law; it is the same today and tomorrow.' What they kept then, they keep today. So one should keep one vow: breathe in and breathe out, thinking, 'May evil, death, not reach me.' If one keeps it, one should keep it to the end. By it one wins union with that deity and a place in its world.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-23.meaning: Keep one simple vow: breathe in and out with awareness. It guards against death.
brihadaranyaka-1-5-23.explanation: Conscious breathing as a spiritual practice.

brihadaranyaka-1-6-1.translation: This world is threefold: name, form and action. For names, speech is their source, for from it all names arise. It is their Saman, for it is equal to all names. It is their Brahman, for it supports all names.
brihadaranyaka-1-6-1.meaning: Everything is name, form or action; speech is the source of all names.
brihadaranyaka-1-6-1.explanation: The world is analysed into three parts.

brihadaranyaka-1-6-2.translation: For forms, the eye is their source, for from it all forms arise. It is their Saman, for it is equal to all forms. It is their Brahman, for it supports all forms.
brihadaranyaka-1-6-2.meaning: The eye is the source of all forms.

brihadaranyaka-1-6-3.translation: For actions, the body is their source, for from it all actions arise. It is their Saman, for it is equal to all actions. It is their Brahman, for it supports all actions. These three are one, the Self; the Self, being one, is these three. This is the immortal covered by the real. Breath is the immortal; name and form are the real. This breath is covered by them.
brihadaranyaka-1-6-3.meaning: Name, form and action are one Self. The immortal life is hidden under names and forms.
brihadaranyaka-1-6-3.explanation: Satya, 'the real', here means the visible world, which covers the immortal.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-1.translation: There was Dripta Balaki, a learned man of the Gargya clan. He said to Ajatashatru, king of Kashi, 'Let me tell you about Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'I will give a thousand cows for such a talk! People run around saying, "Janaka, Janaka!"'
brihadaranyaka-2-1-1.meaning: A proud scholar offers to teach a king about Brahman; the king is delighted.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-1.explanation: Chapter 2 opens with the proud Gargya and the wise king Ajatashatru. The king hopes to rival King Janaka's fame as a patron.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-2.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the sun: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the one who stands above all beings, their head and king.' Whoever worships it so becomes the one above all beings, their head and king.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-2.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the sun; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-2.explanation: The proud scholar Gargya offers twelve definitions of Brahman; the king has already gone beyond each one.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-3.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the moon: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as great King Soma clothed in white.' Whoever worships it so has Soma pressed for him every day, and his food never fails.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-3.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the moon; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-3.explanation: The proud scholar Gargya offers twelve definitions of Brahman; the king has already gone beyond each one.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-4.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in lightning: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the radiant one.' Whoever worships it so becomes radiant, and his children are radiant.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-4.meaning: Gargya worships the person in lightning; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-4.explanation: The proud scholar Gargya offers twelve definitions of Brahman; the king has already gone beyond each one.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-5.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in space: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the full and unmoving.' Whoever worships it so is filled with children and cattle, and his line never dies out.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-5.meaning: Gargya worships the person in space; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-5.explanation: The proud scholar Gargya offers twelve definitions of Brahman; the king has already gone beyond each one.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-6.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the wind: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as Indra Vaikuntha, the unconquered army.' Whoever worships it so becomes victorious, unconquerable, conquering his enemies.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-6.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the wind; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-6.explanation: The proud scholar Gargya offers twelve definitions of Brahman; the king has already gone beyond each one.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-7.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in fire: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the all-conquering.' Whoever worships it so becomes all-conquering, and so do his children.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-7.meaning: Gargya worships the person in fire; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-7.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-8.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in water: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the likeness.' Whoever worships it so finds what is fitting coming to him, not what is unfitting, and fitting children are born to him.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-8.meaning: Gargya worships the person in water; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-8.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-9.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in a mirror: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the shining one.' Whoever worships it so becomes shining, as do his children, and outshines all he meets.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-9.meaning: Gargya worships the person in a mirror; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-9.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-10.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the sound that follows a person as he walks: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as life.' Whoever worships it so lives his full span in this world, and his breath does not leave him before his time.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-10.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the sound that follows a person as he walks; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-10.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-11.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the directions: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the inseparable companion.' Whoever worships it so has companions, and his group is never broken.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-11.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the directions; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-11.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-12.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the shadow: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as death.' Whoever worships it so lives his full span, and death does not come to him before his time.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-12.meaning: Gargya worships the person in the shadow; the king already knows this and more.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-12.explanation: Another of Gargya's partial views of Brahman.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-13.translation: Gargya said, 'The person in the body: that is what I worship as Brahman.' Ajatashatru said, 'Do not speak to me about that! I worship it as the one who has a self.' Whoever worships it so becomes self-possessed, and so do his children. Then Gargya fell silent.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-13.meaning: Gargya's last idea is also already known to the king, and Gargya falls silent.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-13.explanation: The scholar has run out of answers.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-14.translation: Ajatashatru said, 'Is that all?' 'That is all.' 'One does not know Brahman by that much.' Gargya said, 'Let me come to you as a student.'
brihadaranyaka-2-1-14.meaning: The king says this is not enough to know Brahman, and the scholar asks to become his student.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-14.explanation: The proud teacher becomes a humble pupil.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-15.translation: Ajatashatru said, 'It is against the natural order for a brahmin to come to a king to learn about Brahman. But I will make you understand.' Taking him by the hand he got up. They came to a sleeping man. He called to him by these names: 'Great one, clothed in white, King Soma!' The man did not get up. He woke him by pushing him with his hand, and he got up.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-15.meaning: The king takes Gargya to a sleeping man, who does not wake to grand names but only to a touch.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-15.explanation: A demonstration about consciousness in sleep.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-16.translation: Ajatashatru said, 'When this man was asleep, where was this person made of understanding? Where did he come back from?' Gargya did not know.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-16.meaning: The king asks: where was the conscious self while the man slept?
brihadaranyaka-2-1-16.explanation: A key question about the nature of the self.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-17.translation: Ajatashatru said, 'When this man was asleep, this person made of understanding gathered the understanding of the senses by his understanding and lay in the space within the heart. When he takes them in, the person is said to be asleep. Then breath is held, speech is held, the eye is held, the ear is held, the mind is held.'
brihadaranyaka-2-1-17.meaning: In sleep, the conscious self gathers in all the senses and rests in the space of the heart.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-17.explanation: Sleep is the self withdrawing into its own centre.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-18.translation: When he moves about in dreams, those are his worlds. He becomes like a great king or a great brahmin; he goes up and down. As a great king takes his people and moves about his own land as he pleases, so he takes his senses and moves about his own body as he pleases.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-18.meaning: In dreams the self moves through its own body as a king moves through his kingdom.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-18.explanation: Dreams are a world the self creates.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-19.translation: When he is fast asleep and knows nothing at all, he slips through the seventy-two thousand channels called hita that go from the heart to the pericardium, and lies there. As a young man, a great king or a great brahmin might lie at the height of bliss, so he lies.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-19.meaning: In deep dreamless sleep, the self rests in perfect bliss.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-19.explanation: Deep sleep is pictured as the highest bliss of ordinary life.

brihadaranyaka-2-1-20.translation: As a spider moves up its thread, and as tiny sparks fly out from a fire, so from this Self come out all breaths, all worlds, all gods, all beings. Its secret name is 'the real behind the real'. The breaths are real, and it is their reality.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-20.meaning: All things come from the Self like sparks from a fire; it is the truth of truth.
brihadaranyaka-2-1-20.explanation: A famous image of creation. Satyasya satyam, 'the real behind the real'.

brihadaranyaka-2-2-1.translation: Whoever knows the young one with its house, its covering, its post and its rope keeps off seven hateful rivals. The young one is the breath in the middle. This body is its house, the head its covering, breath its post, food its rope.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-1.meaning: Breath is like a calf tied in the body, with food as its rope.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-1.explanation: An image for the life-breath kept in the body.

brihadaranyaka-2-2-2.translation: Seven imperishable powers serve it. Through the red lines in the eye, Rudra serves it; through the water in the eye, the rain-god; through the pupil, the sun; through the dark of the eye, fire; through the white, Indra; through the lower eyelash, the earth; through the upper, heaven. One who knows this never lacks food.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-2.meaning: The gods serve life through the parts of the eye.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-2.explanation: Each part of the eye is linked to a god.

brihadaranyaka-2-2-3.translation: There is this verse: 'There is a bowl with its mouth below and its bottom above. In it is placed glory of every form. On its rim sit seven sages; speech is the eighth, joined with prayer.' The bowl with its mouth below and its bottom above is the head. The glory of every form placed in it is the breaths. The seven sages on its rim are the breaths. Speech is the eighth, joined with prayer.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-3.meaning: The head is like an upside-down bowl; the senses are the seven sages sitting on its rim.

brihadaranyaka-2-2-4.translation: These two (ears) are Gotama and Bharadvaja; this is Gotama, this Bharadvaja. These two (eyes) are Vishvamitra and Jamadagni. These two (nostrils) are Vasishtha and Kashyapa. Speech is Atri, for food is eaten with speech; Atri is really 'atti', the eater. One who knows this eats everything, and everything becomes his food.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-4.meaning: The ears, eyes, nostrils and mouth are the seven great sages.
brihadaranyaka-2-2-4.explanation: Each sense is named after one of the ancient seers.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-1.translation: Brahman has two forms: the formed and the formless, the mortal and the immortal, the still and the moving, the being and the beyond.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-1.meaning: Brahman has two forms: one with shape and one without.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-1.explanation: A key teaching about the two aspects of reality.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-2.translation: The formed is everything other than wind and mid-air. It is mortal, still and being. The essence of this formed, mortal, still being is the sun that burns, for it is the essence of being.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-2.meaning: Everything solid is the formed side; its essence is the sun.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-2.explanation: In nature, the visible world is the formed side.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-3.translation: The formless is wind and mid-air. It is immortal, moving and beyond. Its essence is the person in the sun's orb, for that is the essence of the beyond. So much about the gods.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-3.meaning: Wind and sky are the formless side; its essence is the person in the sun.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-3.explanation: The unseen world is the formless side.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-4.translation: Now about the self. The formed is everything other than breath and the space within the self. It is mortal, still and being. Its essence is the eye, for it is the essence of being.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-4.meaning: In us, the body is the formed side, and its essence is the eye.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-4.explanation: The same analysis applied to a person.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-5.translation: The formless is breath and the space within the self. It is immortal, moving and beyond. Its essence is the person in the right eye, for it is the essence of the beyond.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-5.meaning: Breath and inner space are the formless side; its essence is the person in the eye.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-5.explanation: The seer within the eye is the inner essence.

brihadaranyaka-2-3-6.translation: The form of this person is like a saffron-coloured cloth, like white wool, like a red beetle, like a flame of fire, like a white lotus, like a sudden flash of lightning. The glory of one who knows this flashes like lightning. Now the teaching: 'Not this, not this.' For there is nothing higher than this 'not this'. Its name is 'the real behind the real'. The breaths are real, and it is their reality.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-6.meaning: Brahman can only be described as 'Not this, not this'; nothing is higher.
brihadaranyaka-2-3-6.explanation: 'Neti neti' is the famous method of describing the ultimate by denying every limited description.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-1.translation: 'Maitreyi,' said Yajnavalkya, 'I am about to leave this life as a householder. Let me make a settlement between you and Katyayani.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-1.meaning: Yajnavalkya is about to become a renunciant and wants to divide his property between his two wives.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-1.explanation: The famous dialogue of Yajnavalkya and his wife Maitreyi begins.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-2.translation: Maitreyi said, 'Sir, if this whole earth full of wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?' 'No,' said Yajnavalkya. 'Your life would be like the life of the rich. There is no hope of immortality through wealth.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-2.meaning: Maitreyi asks if wealth can make her immortal; Yajnavalkya says no.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-2.explanation: One of the most famous questions in the Upanishads.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-3.translation: Maitreyi said, 'What would I do with something that cannot make me immortal? Tell me, sir, what you know.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-3.meaning: She refuses the wealth and asks for his wisdom instead.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-4.translation: Yajnavalkya said, 'You have always been dear to me, and now you speak what is dear. Come, sit; I will explain. As I explain, reflect on it deeply.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-4.meaning: Yajnavalkya is moved by her question and agrees to teach her.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-5.translation: He said: 'It is not for love of the husband that the husband is dear, but for love of the Self. It is not for love of the wife that the wife is dear, but for love of the Self. Not for love of children, wealth, the priestly or ruling class, the worlds, the gods, beings, or of all, are they dear, but for love of the Self. It is the Self that should be seen, heard, reflected on and meditated upon, Maitreyi. When the Self is seen, heard, reflected on and understood, all this is known.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-5.meaning: We love everything because of the Self; so the Self is what we should come to know.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-5.explanation: One of the most quoted passages: all love is at root love of the Self. Hearing, reflecting and meditating became the classic three steps of spiritual study.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-6.translation: 'The priestly class abandons one who thinks it is other than the Self. The ruling class, the worlds, the gods, beings, everything abandon one who thinks they are other than the Self. This priestly class, this ruling class, these worlds, these gods, these beings, all this is the Self.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-6.meaning: Whoever sees anything as separate from the Self loses it; everything is the Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-6.explanation: Seeing things as separate leads to loss.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-7.translation: As when a drum is played, one cannot catch its sounds separately, but by catching the drum or its player the sound is caught,
brihadaranyaka-2-4-7.meaning: You cannot catch the sounds of a drum one by one, only by holding the drum itself.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-7.explanation: Yajnavalkya's images: grasp the source and you grasp everything that comes from it. Here the source is the Self.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-8.translation: As when a conch is played, one cannot catch its sounds separately, but by catching the conch or its player the sound is caught,
brihadaranyaka-2-4-8.meaning: You cannot catch the sounds of a conch one by one, only by holding the conch itself.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-8.explanation: Yajnavalkya's images: grasp the source and you grasp everything that comes from it. Here the source is the Self.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-9.translation: As when a lute is played, one cannot catch its sounds separately, but by catching the lute or its player the sound is caught,
brihadaranyaka-2-4-9.meaning: You cannot catch the sounds of a lute one by one, only by holding the lute itself.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-9.explanation: Yajnavalkya's images: grasp the source and you grasp everything that comes from it. Here the source is the Self.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-10.translation: 'As smoke pours out separately from a fire lit with damp wood, so the Rig Veda, Yajur Veda, Sama Veda, Atharvangirasa, histories, ancient lore, sciences, Upanishads, verses, sutras, explanations and commentaries are the breath of this great Being. All these are its breath.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-10.meaning: All sacred knowledge is the breath of the great Being.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-10.explanation: Even the Vedas are not separate from the Self.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-11.translation: 'As the ocean is the meeting place of all waters, so the skin is of all touches, the nose of all smells, the tongue of all tastes, the eye of all forms, the ear of all sounds, the mind of all intentions, the heart of all knowledge, the hands of all actions, the sexual organ of all pleasures, the anus of all excretions, the feet of all journeys, and speech of all the Vedas.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-11.meaning: Each sense gathers its own experiences, as the ocean gathers all waters.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-11.explanation: Everything flows back to a single centre, as rivers to the sea.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-12.translation: 'As a lump of salt thrown into water dissolves and cannot be picked out, yet wherever you taste, it is salty, so this great Being, endless and boundless, is a mass of awareness. It rises from these elements and disappears back into them. After death there is no awareness. This is what I say,' said Yajnavalkya.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-12.meaning: The great Being is pure awareness, like salt dissolved in water; after death there is no separate awareness.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-12.explanation: Like Chandogya 6.13, the Self pervades everything. Individual consciousness dissolves at death.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-13.translation: Maitreyi said, 'Here, sir, you have confused me by saying that after death there is no awareness.' He said, 'I am not saying anything confusing. This is enough for understanding.'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-13.meaning: Maitreyi is puzzled; Yajnavalkya says it will become clear.

brihadaranyaka-2-4-14.translation: 'For where there is duality, as it were, one smells another, one sees another, one hears another, one speaks to another, one thinks of another, one knows another. But where everything has become one's own Self, then by what and whom should one smell, see, hear, speak to, think of, or know? By what can one know that by which one knows all this? By what, my dear, can one know the knower?'
brihadaranyaka-2-4-14.meaning: Awareness of 'others' needs two; when all is the Self, there is no other. And no one can know the knower itself.
brihadaranyaka-2-4-14.explanation: A profound teaching: the knower can never be an object of knowledge.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-1.translation: This earth is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this earth and the shining, immortal person in the body in oneself are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-1.meaning: This earth and all beings feed each other like honey; the light in it and in us is the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-1.explanation: The 'honey doctrine' (madhu vidya): everything is interdependent, and the same Self shines in all.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-2.translation: These waters is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for these waters. The shining, immortal person in these waters and the shining, immortal person in the semen in oneself are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-2.meaning: These waters and all beings feed each other like honey; the light in it and in us is the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-2.explanation: The 'honey doctrine' (madhu vidya): everything is interdependent, and the same Self shines in all.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-3.translation: This fire is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this fire and the shining, immortal person made of speech in oneself are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-3.meaning: This fire and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light made of speech in oneself are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-3.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-4.translation: This wind is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this wind and the shining, immortal person that is breath in oneself are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-4.meaning: This wind and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light that is breath in oneself are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-4.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-5.translation: This sun is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this sun and the shining, immortal person in the eye are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-5.meaning: This sun and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in the eye are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-5.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-6.translation: These directions is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in these directions and the shining, immortal person in the ear and in the echo are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-6.meaning: These directions and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in the ear and in the echo are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-6.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-7.translation: This moon is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this moon and the shining, immortal person in the mind are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-7.meaning: This moon and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in the mind are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-7.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-8.translation: This lightning is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this lightning and the shining, immortal person in one's own radiance are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-8.meaning: This lightning and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in one's own radiance are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-8.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-9.translation: This thunder is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this thunder and the shining, immortal person in sound and tone are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-9.meaning: This thunder and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in sound and tone are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-9.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-10.translation: This space is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this space and the shining, immortal person in the space of the heart are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-10.meaning: This space and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in the space of the heart are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-10.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-11.translation: This dharma is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this dharma and the shining, immortal person in one's own sense of right are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-11.meaning: This dharma and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in one's own sense of right are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-11.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-12.translation: This truth is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this truth and the shining, immortal person in one's own truthfulness are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-12.meaning: This truth and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in one's own truthfulness are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-12.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-13.translation: This humanity is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for it. The shining, immortal person in this humanity and the shining, immortal person in oneself as a human being are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-13.meaning: This humanity and all beings feed each other; the light in it and the light in oneself as a human being are the same Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-13.explanation: The honey teaching continues: every part of nature is linked to a part of us, and the same Self shines in both.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-14.translation: This Self is honey for all beings, and all beings are honey for this Self. The shining, immortal person in this Self and the shining, immortal Self itself are one: this Self. This is the immortal, this is Brahman, this is all.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-14.meaning: The Self and all beings are honey to each other; everything is one Self.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-14.explanation: The honey teaching reaches its peak: the Self itself.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-15.translation: This Self is the ruler of all, the king of all beings. As the spokes are fixed in the hub and rim of a wheel, so in this Self all beings, all gods, all worlds, all breaths, all these selves are fixed.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-15.meaning: The Self holds all things together, like the hub of a wheel holds its spokes.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-16.translation: This is the honey that Dadhyanch Atharvana taught the two Ashvins. Seeing this, the sage said: 'O heroes, I reveal your mighty deed for gain, as thunder reveals the rain: the honey that Dadhyanch Atharvana told you through a horse's head.'
brihadaranyaka-2-5-16.meaning: The Ashvins learned the honey teaching from a sage speaking through a horse's head.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-16.explanation: A Rig Veda verse is quoted about the sage Dadhyanch, who taught the honey teaching through a horse's head.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-17.translation: This is the honey that Dadhyanch Atharvana taught the two Ashvins. Seeing this, the sage said: 'O Ashvins, you put a horse's head on Dadhyanch Atharvana. Keeping his word, he told you the honey of Tvashtri, your secret, O wonder-workers.'
brihadaranyaka-2-5-17.meaning: The Ashvins gave the sage a horse's head so he could teach them safely.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-17.explanation: A Rig Veda verse is quoted about the sage Dadhyanch, who taught the honey teaching through a horse's head.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-18.translation: This is the honey that Dadhyanch Atharvana taught the Ashvins. Seeing this, the sage said: 'He made bodies with two feet, he made bodies with four. Having first become a bird, the Person entered the bodies.' This Person dwells in all bodies (puri-shaya). There is nothing not covered by him, nothing not filled by him.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-18.meaning: The Person entered every body; nothing is outside him.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-18.explanation: Word-play: purusha as puri-shaya, 'dwelling in the city' of the body.

brihadaranyaka-2-5-19.translation: This is the honey that Dadhyanch Atharvana taught the Ashvins. Seeing this, the sage said: 'He took the form of every form; that form is his to be seen. Indra moves in many forms by his powers; his horses are yoked, a hundred and ten.' He is the horses; he is the tens and thousands, many and endless. This Brahman has no before and no after, no inside and no outside. This Self is Brahman, experiencing all. This is the teaching.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-19.meaning: The one Self takes every form; it has no inside or outside. This Self is Brahman.
brihadaranyaka-2-5-19.explanation: 'Ayam atma brahma', 'This Self is Brahman', is another of the four great sayings.

brihadaranyaka-2-6-1.translation: Now the line of teachers. Pautimashya received it from Gaupavana; Gaupavana from Paushtimashya; Paushtimashya from Gaupavana; Gaupavana from Kaushika; Kaushika from Kaundinya; Kaundinya from Shandilya; Shandilya from Kaushika and Gautama; Gautama
brihadaranyaka-2-6-1.meaning: A list of the teachers who passed this teaching down.
brihadaranyaka-2-6-1.explanation: Lineage lists (vamsha) honour the chain of teachers. This is mainly a list of names.

brihadaranyaka-2-6-2.translation: from Agniveshya; Agniveshya from Shandilya and Anabhimlata; Anabhimlata from Anabhimlata; Anabhimlata from Anabhimlata; Anabhimlata from Gautama; Gautama from Saitava and Prachinayogya; they from Parasharya; Parasharya from Bharadvaja; Bharadvaja from Bharadvaja and Gautama; Gautama from Bharadvaja; Bharadvaja from Parasharya; Parasharya from Vaijavapayana; Vaijavapayana from Kaushikayani; Kaushikayani

brihadaranyaka-2-6-3.translation: from Ghritakaushika; ... Atharvan Daiva from Mrityu Pradhvamsana; ... Parameshthin from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent. Homage to Brahman.
brihadaranyaka-2-6-3.meaning: The chain of teachers goes back through many sages to Brahman itself. Homage to Brahman.
brihadaranyaka-2-6-3.explanation: The list ends at Brahman, the self-existent source of all teaching.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-1.translation: Janaka, king of Videha, held a sacrifice with rich gifts. Brahmins from the Kuru and Panchala lands gathered there. Janaka wanted to know which of them was the most learned. He set apart a thousand cows, with ten gold coins tied to the horns of each.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-1.meaning: King Janaka offers a thousand cows with gold to the most learned scholar.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-1.explanation: Chapter 3 begins: the great debate at Janaka's court, where Yajnavalkya faces many challengers.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-2.translation: He said, 'Honoured brahmins, let the one who is the best knower of Brahman drive these cows away.' The brahmins did not dare. Then Yajnavalkya said to his own student, 'Samashravas, dear, drive them away.' He drove them away. The brahmins were angry: 'How can he call himself the best knower of Brahman among us?' Janaka's hotri priest Ashvala asked him, 'Yajnavalkya, are you really the best knower of Brahman among us?' He replied, 'We bow to the best knower of Brahman. We just want the cows!' Then Ashvala decided to question him.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-2.meaning: Yajnavalkya boldly takes the prize, joking that he just wants the cows; the others challenge him.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-2.explanation: Yajnavalkya's humour and confidence. The questioning begins.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-3.translation: 'Yajnavalkya,' he said, 'since all this is reached by death, overcome by death, by what means does the sacrificer free himself from death's reach?' 'By the hotri priest, by fire, by speech. Speech is the hotri of the sacrifice. This speech is fire, the hotri; that is freedom, that is complete freedom.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-3.meaning: Freedom from death comes through speech, which is fire.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-3.explanation: Each priest of the sacrifice is linked to a power that frees from limitation.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-4.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, since all this is reached by day and night, by what means does the sacrificer free himself from them?' 'By the adhvaryu priest, by the eye, by the sun. The eye is the adhvaryu of the sacrifice. This eye is the sun, the adhvaryu; that is freedom, that is complete freedom.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-4.meaning: Freedom from day and night comes through the eye, which is the sun.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-5.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, since all this is reached by the bright and dark halves of the month, by what means does the sacrificer free himself from them?' 'By the udgatri priest, by wind, by breath. Breath is the udgatri of the sacrifice. This breath is wind, the udgatri; that is freedom, that is complete freedom.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-5.meaning: Freedom from the moon's phases comes through breath, which is wind.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-6.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, since the mid-air seems to have no support, by what ladder does the sacrificer climb to heaven?' 'By the brahman priest, by the mind, by the moon. The mind is the brahman of the sacrifice. This mind is the moon, the brahman; that is freedom, that is complete freedom.' These are the freedoms. Now the attainments.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-6.meaning: The mind, which is the moon, is the ladder to heaven.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-7.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, with how many Rik verses will the hotri perform in this sacrifice today?' 'With three.' 'Which three?' 'The introductory verse, the offering verse, and the praise verse as the third.' 'What does he win with them?' 'Whatever has breath.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-7.meaning: The hotri uses three verses and wins all living beings.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-7.explanation: Ashvala's questions move to ritual details.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-8.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, how many offerings will the adhvaryu make today?' 'Three.' 'Which three?' 'Those that blaze up when offered, those that make a great noise, and those that sink down.' 'What does he win with them?' 'With those that blaze up, the world of the gods, for it shines; with those that make noise, the world of the ancestors, for it is noisy; with those that sink down, the human world, for it is below.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-8.meaning: Three kinds of offering win the worlds of gods, ancestors and humans.
brihadaranyaka-3-1-8.explanation: Each kind of offering matches a world.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-9.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, with how many deities does the brahman priest guard the sacrifice from the south today?' 'With one.' 'Which one?' 'The mind. The mind is endless, and the All-gods are endless. With it he wins an endless world.'
brihadaranyaka-3-1-9.meaning: The mind alone guards the rite, and since it is endless it wins an endless world.

brihadaranyaka-3-1-10.translation: 'Yajnavalkya, how many hymns of praise will the udgatri sing today?' 'Three.' 'Which three?' 'The introductory, the offering, and the praise as the third.'
